name: mia-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017
title: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 — EXL3 2.9 bpw on TensorFold (Mia's AI Lab)
author: Mia's AI Lab, on BertholomusAI's TensorFold fork
engine: TensorFold native (Zig), image built on node A

measured.note: the source's numbers: prose, temperature 0, thinking off, CONTEXT=524288, both GPUs at 2,200 MHz; code 118.1 tok/s at one stream; prefill ~2,150 tok/s from 4K to 256K tokens

requirements: scripts/local.sh in the checkout (copy scripts/local.sh.example) with WORKER=<user>@<node B's CX7 address>.
Key-based ssh from node A to node B, and Docker with the NVIDIA runtime on both; git, python3 and the hf CLI on node A.
An NFS export of node A's Hugging Face cache to node B (the kit's docs/requirements.md): node B reads the checkpoint over it.
Disk: ~505 GB plus ~25 GB for the image on node A, ~310 GB on node B.
112 GiB MemAvailable on each Spark when it starts (the kit's own check). With other software on node A, CONTEXT=524288 is the practical limit.
The same GPU clock ceiling on both Sparks (nvidia-smi -lgc 0,2200): the slower GPU sets the pace.
notes: The first start builds the engine image (two Zig builds, ~6 minutes), downloads the checkpoint (196 GiB) and Engram's tables (~203 GB), writes each rank's weight file and copies the tables to node B.
Run `tsm kit prepare` while no large model is loaded: writing the two ~106 GB weight files competes for the Sparks' shared memory.
The API thinks before it answers unless a request turns thinking off; give replies enough max_tokens.
